text: American Place Casino is a convenience-led, locals-first gaming and entertainment property in Waukegan that operates from a temporary facility while a permanent casino is developed [14][15][16][11]. Gaming is the core revenue engine, with sportsbook, poker, dining, entertainment, and events used to deepen trip frequency, dwell time, and wallet share [11][18][19][20][22][23][18][24][20][25][26]. The growth path is to tighten rated-play capture and repeat visitation on the current asset, then unlock higher earning capacity through a larger permanent floor and an event-led venue overlay [28][30][31][34][35][36][30][37][13]. The operating model has a financial baseline of $89.4M of EBITDA, with a 27.3% margin on $328.0M of revenue [10][5][1][2]. Key diligence question: whether the permanent-format transition can happen quickly enough, and with enough CRM precision, to let a temporary property close share gaps as newer Illinois casinos reset customer expectations [6][7][8][9][27].

text: American Place is a locals-first casino built to turn repeat visits into on-site spending. It makes money mainly from casino gaming [11][18], then adds revenue from sports wagering, poker, dining, entertainment, and private events [19][51][20][26]. The model works because local drive-in guests can be pushed to stay longer and spend more across the property, so the buyer should view the business as dependent on repeat regional demand and on the permanent casino plan being delivered on time [13][17][11].

text: American Casino reached $328.0M of net revenue in 2005A, but the 7.8% CAGR masks an uneven path that peaked at 14.2% in 2004A before easing to 9.3% in 2005A. Growth was still concentrated: Stratosphere accounted for 49.8% of the achieved increase from 2003A to 2005A, so the revenue base broadened only modestly. Profitability improved to a 27.3% adjusted EBITDA margin, and the nil identified add-backs in 2005A suggest the latest earnings are backed by booked performance rather than adjustment-heavy reporting. Looking ahead, management's 2008 plan of $472.8M would need acquisition-led upside and sustained operating acceleration to close the gap to the published base and upside cases.
